campaign_note: Google GTIG/Mandiant reported that suspected PRC-nexus cluster UNC6201 exploited the hard-coded credential since at least mid-2024 to deploy SLAYSTYLE, BRICKSTORM and GRIMBOLT; Mandiant put the victim count at under a dozen organizations.

evidence.counts_what: organizations known to Mandiant to be impacted by UNC6201 exploitation of CVE-2026-22769 (upper bound, not an exact count)
evidence.measured_by: Mandiant Consulting (Rich Reece), quoted by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: We are aware of less than a dozen impacted organizations

evidence.counts_what: earliest identified exploitation activity (zero-day dwell of roughly 18 months before disclosure)
evidence.quote: The earliest identified exploitation activity of this vulnerability occurred in mid-2024.

campaign_note: Exploit attempts against PostgreSQL-backed Drupal sites began within about two days of the 2026-05-20 fix; Imperva characterized most activity as probing and no compromise counts were found.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Drupal Security Team advisory update (SA-CORE-2026-004), as reported by The Hacker News

evidence.counts_what: attack attempts (lower bound, 'over 15,000') targeting almost 6,000 individual sites across 65 countries; mostly probing; not a compromise count
evidence.measured_by: Imperva (Thales), reported by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: observed over 15,000 attack attempts targeting almost 6,000 individual sites across 65 countries

evidence.counts_what: individual sites targeted by attack attempts ('almost 6,000'); targeted, not compromised
evidence.measured_by: Imperva (Thales), reported by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: observed over 15,000 attack attempts targeting almost 6,000 individual sites across 65 countries

campaign_note: Disclosed October 2025 as a DoS, re-categorized by F5 to unauthenticated RCE in March 2026 with confirmed exploitation; no victim or compromise counts published, only Shadowserver fingerprint counts of exposed BIG-IP APM.

evidence.counts_what: IPs with BIG-IP APM fingerprints (exposed product, not confirmed vulnerable configuration); 'over 17,100'; article dated 2026-04-02 says 'on Wednesday'
evidence.quote: Shadowserver said on Wednesday that it now tracks over 17,100 IPs with BIG-IP APM fingerprints.

evidence.counts_what: IPs with F5 BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online (exposed product, not confirmed vulnerable); 'over 14,100'; US 5138, Europe 4750, Asia 2689; article dated 2026-04-06
evidence.quote: tracking over 14,100 IPs with F5 BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online

evidence.counts_what: BIG-IP instances of any module exposed online (exposed product, broader than APM, not confirmed vulnerable); 'over 240,000'; article dated 2026-03-30

campaign_note: F5 disclosed the APM OAuth heap overflow on 2026-09-22 as already exploited; no attribution, victim or compromise counts found, only a Shadowserver fingerprint count of exposed BIG-IP APM.

first_exploitation_claim.source: F5 security advisory K000162605, as reported by BleepingComputer

evidence.counts_what: IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints (exposed product; not confirmed to have the vulnerable access policy plus OAuth profile configuration); 'over 14,700'; 'currently' as of article dated 2026-09-23
evidence.quote: Shadowserver currently tracks over 14,700 IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints.

campaign_note: Attackers used two malicious FortiCloud SSO accounts to log into other customers' FortiGates, download configurations and create local admin accounts; Fortinet says only that a small number of customers reported it.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Fortinet customer reports, per BleepingComputer (Arctic Wolf bulletin same day; Fortinet PSIRT blog 2026-01-22)

evidence.counts_what: customers reporting unexpected login activity on their devices (unquantified)
evidence.quote: a small number of customers reported unexpected login activity occurring on their devices

evidence.counts_what: malicious FortiCloud SSO accounts used by the attackers (attacker infrastructure, not victims)
evidence.quote: two malicious FortiCloud SSO accounts, which were locked out on January 22

campaign_note: Zero-day exploitation of the EMS access-control flaw was seen by Defused Cyber and on watchTowr honeypots from 2026-03-31, days after CVE-2026-21643 came under attack; it is not known whether the same actor is behind both.

first_exploitation_claim.source: watchTowr honeypots, as reported by The Hacker News

evidence.counts_what: publicly accessible FortiClient EMS instances globally (exposed product, not confirmed vulnerable); 'over 2,000' in one sentence and 'approximately 2,000' in another; article dated 2026-04-06; secondary outlet outside the brief's named press list
evidence.measured_by: Shadowserver, reported by Cyber Security News
evidence.quote: identifying over 2,000 publicly accessible instances globally

campaign_note: The EMS SQL injection came under active exploitation days before CVE-2026-35616 was disclosed; no first-exploitation date or victim count was found.

first_exploitation_claim.source: The Hacker News (2026-04-05 article says the flaw had come under active exploitation days earlier; no date or original reporter given)

evidence.counts_what: publicly accessible FortiClient EMS instances globally (exposed product, not confirmed vulnerable; same figure as recorded for CVE-2026-35616); article dated 2026-04-06; secondary outlet outside the brief's named press list
evidence.measured_by: Shadowserver, reported by Cyber Security News
evidence.quote: identifying over 2,000 publicly accessible instances globally
